authority: Proposed; pending user approval. Motivated by 15 live runs (2026-09) and the sketch design that the dispatcher, not the driving LLM, runs the evidence chain (S4.1-S4.2, S4.6, S4.8; S4.2 section 7 for recovery).
classification: architecture regression: LLM-mediated hops (facade projection of S4.1-S4.2), not a policy change
input_and_actual: Across 15 live runs the facade tools were 13% of agent wall time (138 s of 1,099 s); the other 87% was the driving LLM (about 2.9 s per turn, 374 turns). The facade exposed read, choose, act, verify and finish as separate MCP tools, so the LLM mediated every hop: a clean booking took 9 LLM-visible calls where native tools take about 5. Nothing in the repo noticed the drift. Live test of the first cua_do (Sonnet 5.5, real Chrome): booking took 8 LLM-visible calls and 20 turns (native 8 calls, 18 turns), orders 13 calls and 33 turns (native 6 and 14). Causes: (1) with eight tools visible the LLM called cua_windows and cua_observe itself before cua_do; (2) cua_do deferred records_ambiguous on BOTH real pages because Chrome advertises AXPress on every static text, cell and row, so discovery keyed on repeated press-capable nodes and listed every repeated element; (3) orders rows have two buttons (Track, Cancel) and cua_do had no way to name one; (4) the LLM never passed expect, so verification fell to the screenshot model, which answered unknown; (5) cua_choose exact answered exact_target_not_unique for "Yes, cancel order" while cua_do found it unique: the dialog buttons had no AXPress in that snapshot, so exact mode (press-capable nodes only) saw the control as absent; the confirm dialog is page content, not an AXSheet. Independent review of the live-shape fixes found shapes the two captured trees did not cover: a success toast with an Undo button read as a confirm dialog (a successful booking deferred, or with confirm="Undo" pressed Undo); per-record labels ("Book Dr A") and single-record pages ended in records_ambiguous with a record_ids hint a cua_do-only caller cannot use; 5+ control dialogs missed by a 1..4 cutoff and a list gaining a card read as a one-control dialog; identity defaulting to all fields deferred the normal orders flow; verify-only and the click path accepted button labels and pre-existing text as proof; a disabled matching record was reported as "no record satisfies the predicates". Live suite (Sonnet 5.5, real Chrome, small suite, ONE run per cell, so n=1 and not a rate): (1) booking: the LLM wrote predicates blind (duration contains "30"), the correct slot reads "half-hour", the predicate excluded it and the chooser picked among five leftovers: a SILENT WRONG CLICK reported done in one call; (2) canvas: two Export buttons drawn on a canvas (labelled by Toolbar and Footer texts) ended control_not_found/dead_end although Perception was healthy.
corrected_behavior: cua_do runs the chain server-side in one call (observe, read, same-record filter, chooser only if several remain, bind, act with S4.8 revalidation, independent verify) and recovers in bounded deterministic code: stale UI or shifted indices reobserve and re-run the whole pipeline with a NEW selection (at most 2 passes, never reusing a stale selection or its tokens, a different fresh pick is a real change and defers); a pre-click Driver/provider failure is retried once after a short backoff (never a click); an unknown field is re-read once; verification escalates AX, then Perception (never satisfying on digits), then the screenshot model; a dialog after the click is never pressed unless the caller opted in with confirm=<exact label>, the dialog's displayed identity matches the selected record completely and exactly one enabled control in the new dialog has that label (never the chooser; otherwise it defers confirm_dialog_present, and a pre-existing, replaced or extra dialog defers confirm_dialog_ambiguous); after a stale refusal recovery requires a complete, unique record identity or it defers record_changed_unverifiable; expect text already on the page before the click, or the text just typed, is unproven and never done; once any click is delivered no selection is handed back; a hard cap of 3x budget_s counts click time too. It returns deferred/failed to the LLM only for (A) a click that may have been delivered but could not be verified, (B) ambiguity (several eligible records, an unknown competitor without accept_unknown, records_ambiguous) and (C) a real content change inside the bound scope that alters which record matches. A clean run is 1 LLM-visible call as MEASURED through the real server tools under a minimal LLM policy (the response reports follow_up_needed, not a call count); specialists still do all reading, matching and choosing. The primitives remain as Advanced escape hatches with unchanged behavior. CALL_BUDGET.json, scripts/check_call_budget.py, a skill lint and the live scorer keep it that way. Live fixes: only cua_do is registered by default (the eight primitives need CUA_TASK_ADVANCED=1) and no deferral or hint ever sends the caller to a primitive; every deferral carries what a second cua_do needs; records are keyed on the repeated ACTIONABLE control inside the page content (button/link/menu item/radio/checkbox roles, AXColumn copies skipped), never repeated static text; control names which button per record (control_needed lists only those labels); expect is a required schema parameter (null ends delivered_unverified, never done); operation="verify" re-checks without clicking; a confirm dialog is detected as new page content (not by role), identified from its own new text, and a control without a press action is reobserved once then deferred (control_not_pressable); cua_choose exact gains an additive diagnostic instead of a misleading "not unique". Review fixes: expect is checked FIRST and only against text-bearing non-control nodes in the page content (never a button label, never present-before, verify-only answers observed, presence only); a dialog is a region (all-new sibling subtrees, role-tagged or >= 2 controls, not list growth), so toasts and grown lists are not dialogs and 5/8-button dialogs are; identity defaults to the fields the eq predicates constrain and a partially shown identity defers confirm_identity_partial with the exact records.identity for next time; discovery falls back to structure (per-record labels) and a single actionable candidate, control matches exactly or by whole-word prefix, and every hint uses only cua_do parameters; a disabled matching record defers record_disabled, several top-level web areas defer web_area_ambiguous, and a page with nothing to press returns dead_end with report_to_user. The budget is measured with a scripted LLM that knows only goal, expect and predicates and learns the rest from deferrals; it covers the shape corpus. No tree captured from an unrelated real site exists yet (capturing one needs the user's consent), so the budgets remain fixture-derived. Live-suite fixes: an incomparable value (shape mismatch with the predicate, or an outlier of the field's shape) is UNKNOWN, never excluded (S4.2 s4), and unknown competitors defer with the strings; the caller answers with accept_unknown (they do not match) or treat_as_match (they do; a controller verdict limited to unknown records, traced judgment controller); evidence.excluded_values audits what predicates threw away (bounded); on pixel-only pages with healthy Perception, control or a quoted label resolves against text regions exactly and uniquely with the near-edit veto, several exact matches defer region_ambiguous and the near parameter (nearest text above or left) picks one; dead_end only when no fallback can help.
tempting_wrong_repair: A lean path that drops specialist offloading (the LLM reads and picks itself); speeding up the specialists (they are 13% of the time); merging tools without a budget so the count creeps back; making cua_do call the chooser for grounded singletons or read twice; letting recovery rebind the consumed selection or loop until stable; retrying a click or anything after a click may have been delivered; treating delivery or an unknown verification as success; dumping the full observation into the response. Also: confirming a dialog because its identity matches, or because its only control is the affirmative one; handing a selection back after a click; recovering by empty or non-unique identity; counting text that was already on the page as proof; a call-count literal in the response; a harness that makes one call per scenario by construction; budgets that count only non-click time. Also: defining a record by any press-capable node; keeping eight tools visible and hoping the LLM stays on cua_do; hints that say use cua_choose or cua_verify; an optional expect; detecting dialogs only by AXSheet/AXDialog role; validating only against tidy synthetic fixtures. Also: treating any new controls as a dialog; letting identity text inside a toast authorize a control; a count cutoff for dialog size; identity defaulting to all fields; counting button labels or pre-existing text as proof; hints that ask for record_ids; a budget policy that already knows control, identity and labels. Also: treating a value that does not match as a value that is excluded; ignoring value shape; letting the chooser pick among the leftovers while a possible competitor is unknown; a treat_as_match that can revive excluded records; clicking the first exact region when several match; ignoring near; dead_end on a canvas that Perception could resolve.

adjacent_holes: Live A/B against the native arm is pending; the budgets are fake-fixture ceilings, not measured live accuracy. Regions mode inside cua_do relies on Perception being healthy and on quoted-label corroboration. A dialog after a non-record click cannot be identity-checked and defers, and any dialog is only pressed with an explicit confirm label. Post-click verification observes again (one extra Driver observation) rather than reusing the act revalidation snapshot. The sketch text is unchanged; proposed wording for S4.2 section 7 (the recovery table) is in the branch report. Expect text present before the click is never proof, even if the click did change the page; an outcome that reuses pre-existing text needs a different expect or the primitives. Confirm-dialog detection is a content diff bounded to 1-4 new controls in the web area: a dialog with more controls, or one rendered outside the web area, is not detected as a dialog. AX action advertisement varies between snapshots; one bounded reobserve is the only mitigation. The live A/B against the native arm must be rerun with the primitives hidden before the one-call claim is measured rather than modeled. Still unproven: no captured tree from an unrelated real site (needs the user's consent), so the shape corpus is synthetic and every budget is fixture-derived. Structural discovery treats same-shaped siblings as records; two same-shaped unrelated regions would be read as records (fails closed on missing control or identity). A dialog that is not a sibling run of new nodes (an overlay re-parenting existing nodes) is not detected. The live findings are n=1 per cell: they show the failures occur, not their rate, and the fixes are validated offline against a real booking tree and SYNTHETIC canvas parse results, not a live canvas. The shape guard is deliberately conservative (a digit-free predicate against digit-bearing strings, such as contains "AM" against clock times, makes every record unknown and defers). Region resolution is exact-text over OCR; a label OCR reads wrongly (and has no near-edit twin) is simply not found.

authority: Proposed; pending user approval. Solution-space decision approved by the user: option B, LOOK then PLAN ONCE then a deterministic executor, with NuExtract3 (not a Qwen/fast-model loop) the only model on the common path. Motivated by the live n=1 A/B (Sonnet 5.5, real Chrome, one run per cell) and by the sketch design that the dispatcher, not the driving LLM, runs the evidence chain (S4.1-S4.2, S4.6, S4.8; S4.2 section 7 for recovery).
classification: architecture change to the default path (facade projection of S4.1-S4.2, S4.6-S4.8), not a policy change: one read-only default tool (cua_look) and a plan grammar for cua_do; SKETCH.md is unchanged (proposed wording in the branch report).
input_and_actual: Live A/B (Sonnet 5.5, real Chrome, n=1 per cell, so not a rate): the single-tool cua_do cut turns from 6-7 to 3-5 but cost 4-6x, and on the booking task the LLM wrote its filter BLIND (duration contains "30") while the correct slot was displayed as "half-hour": cua_do booked a decoy and reported done. A filter written without seeing the page is the failure class. Option D (a fast model choosing every step) failed for a different reason (it lost the task state) and costs 1-3 s per step. The measured budget (CE-FACADE-003) was one LLM-visible call and assumed the LLM already knew the strings.
corrected_behavior: The LLM SEES the page once, then plans once, and the server executes deterministically. (1) cua_look (default tool, read-only, no click, no window move, NO model by default) returns the strings the page displays: record_kind, records[{r, controls, lines <= 6 x 60 chars}], page text, dialogs, other controls, inputs, header, canvas.text_regions only when AX has no pressable page controls and Perception is healthy, counts, truncated{records, lines, bytes}, notes (never a silent cut), a look_id (a short hash of the ordered displayed record lines) and ms_by_stage; focus filters records lexically and reports how many it left out; fields (optional) adds NuExtract values per record in chunks of 10 through the existing read path. (2) cua_do(steps=[...], look_id, abort_if) accepts a plan of up to 10 steps (press | type | confirm | verify), mutually exclusive with the single-step arguments, validated WHOLE before any Driver action: every press/type/confirm step has a non-null expect (null only on the last step, ending delivered_unverified), type has text, confirm is only an explicit step directly after a press and needs an exact label, a control label with a destructive verb (delete/remove/erase/discard/reset/sign out) the plan goal lacks is refused (again on the RESOLVED control at execution), unknown do/keys are refused. A record filter over displayed lines (where.lines, conjunctive eq/contains/neq/not_contains) is allowed ONLY with a look_id the server issued for this window, and only while the page still reads the same (the displayed lines are recomputed and rehashed; a mismatch defers page_changed_since_look before any click); only records the look displayed can match; none or several matches defer and the chooser is never asked. where.fields keeps the NuExtract path with the shape/incomparable->unknown rule, treat_as_match/accept_unknown and the excluded_values audit. (3) Each step is one run of the existing single-step machinery on a fresh observation (discovery, filter, bind, act with scope revalidation, per-step recovery: a stale refusal re-runs THAT step with a NEW selection, a pre-click failure is retried once, a click is never retried, no selection after a delivered click), verified by its expect (text-bearing non-control nodes only); the plan stops at the first non-done step; abort_if stops it when its text appears in a fresh observation. An explicit confirm step presses a dialog control only if the dialog is the only new one, displays EVERY string of the selected record identity (identity texts, default the values the plan required) and holds exactly one control with that exact label. The response is small: status done|stopped|aborted|refused|failed (+ delivered_unverified, observed), failed_step, steps[{n, do, status, selected{description}, verification{status, route}, ms}], a compact summary, delivery, follow_up_needed and a hint carrying only cua_look/cua_do parameters. The primitives stay hidden unless CUA_TASK_ADVANCED=1; D is untouched. CALL_BUDGET.json now names cua_do and cua_look as the default path and measures look-then-plan scenarios through the real server tools with a scripted LLM that starts knowing only the goal and expect. REVIEW OF PR 18 (the look_id guard narrowed the blind-filter failure, it did not close it): the look_id now hashes the window title, the headings and the FULL untruncated lines of the displayed records (hidden text changes it; a lone toast does not) and is stored per (pid, window_id, hash); negative conditions (not_contains, neq) are refused over records whose lines were cut or omitted (negative_condition_over_cut_lines); identity strings must be whole tokens of the dialog lines and a line carrying an identity with a negation defers confirm_dialog_negated; a destructive control (delete, remove, erase, discard, reset, sign out, cancel subscription) needs the step own allow_destructive naming the exact label and goal text never unlocks it (validation and resolved control); plan steps match control EXACTLY unless control_match is prefix; every look carries untrusted_page_text true and a fixed notice; Facade.subtree child-map equivalence and cache invalidation are tested. SECOND REVIEW OF PR 18 (the remaining breaks were word lists and displayed-subset uniqueness; the fix is not longer lists): (1) where.lines uniqueness is decided over ALL records of the fresh observation, so a capped or focused look cannot turn an ambiguous condition into a click (where_matches_several with match_count and displayed_matches). (2) A confirm step must declare dialog_text, the COMPLETE text lines of the dialog; nothing is pressed unless the dialog shows exactly those lines (confirm_dialog_unexpected_text shows the actual lines otherwise): POSITIVE AUTHORIZATION replaces the negation word list, which is deleted; the exact confirm label and the whole-token identity check remain as sanity checks. EXPECTED COST: the dialog wording is usually unknown until it appears, so a confirm plan is press, defer with the actual dialog lines, then a deliberate press of the dialog control (3 calls measured; 2 only when the wording is known). (3) The destructive-label list for press/type controls is widened (delete, remove, erase, discard, reset, clear, wipe, purge, drop, destroy, uninstall, empty trash, move to trash, overwrite, deactivate, terminate, revoke, unsubscribe, disconnect, close account, cancel subscription, log out, sign out) and is a FLOOR that cannot be complete in every language and phrasing: the dialog whitelist is the real backstop. (4) cua_look gains max_lines (default 6, max 20) and line_chars (default 60, max 200); selecting a record that had cut or omitted lines defers selected_record_has_hidden_text unless the step carries accept_hidden_text true (a shown positive match cannot rule out a contradicting hidden line). (5) The look_id also covers every page control label, value, enabled and checked/selected state; a press on a toggle-like control (checkbox, radio, switch) needs a look_id of a look that saw its state and stops page_changed_since_look or toggle_state_unseen otherwise. (6) Every cua_do response and every look carries untrusted_page_text true and the fixed notice; hints never contain page text. THIRD REVIEW OF PR 18 (the last offline round: what counts as page text must be REGION-COMPLETE): a confirm step declares dialog_text AND dialog_controls; the dialog region (every new node in the window with subtrees, the container holding the dialog cluster, the nearest dialog-tagged ancestor) is compared in full: text of ANY role (image and group labels, field and text-area values, container text) and EVERY control with its state (Also delete my account [checked]); any undeclared text, control or state defers confirm_dialog_unexpected_text with the actual lines and controls; text already inside the container (identical to page text) is still compared. Record lines carry tagged image:, group:, field: and state: lines and text the look cannot represent counts as hidden (accept_hidden_text, negative conditions refused). The look_id hashes structural paths (role and same-role ordinal, never indices) and every input value, chosen option and exposed ARIA state, so a banner before the list does not change it and a quantity change does. Every look and cua_do response on every path carries the untrusted marker and fixed messages. The destructive list adds buy, purchase, pay, send, publish, transfer, refund, void, submit/place order, confirm payment and matches on FOLDED text (NFKC, zero-width, diacritics, casefold, Cyrillic/Greek look-alikes); Disconnected and Removed items (3) do not match; Clear filter and Reset zoom do (documented friction). The list is a FLOOR; the dialog whitelist is the backstop. LIVE-ONLY: real Chrome exposure of images, groups, ARIA state and input values, and where real dialogs attach (see docs/PLAN-B.md). LIVE CAPTURE 2026-09-28 (read-only, no clicks; all 17 suite pages, real Driver.observe, real Perception parse on the canvas pages; sanitized fixtures in facade/fixtures/real, tests in facade/test_real_pages.py): the Driver exposes only actions, depth, element_index, element_token, enabled, frame, in_web_content, label, parent_index, role, screenshot_frame, selected and value, so the checked/expanded/pressed/current/busy keys the look and look_id also cover are INERT on real Chrome (documented as such); radio and checkbox state is read from value 0/1 and selected. Trees were complete (invoices 2,459 elements in 0.78 s), no page virtualized, no AXGroup or dialog role inside web content. The capture found three defects in the shared record inference, fixed with tests first: heading LEVEL values and the window-title heading leaked into the first record of a flat list (a where.lines contains Contacts selected record 1), selected:false noise on every plain button, heading levels in the page text; plus the invoices look overshot max_bytes (6015 > 6000). Still UNVERIFIED because no captured page has a checkbox or a dialog: where real dialogs attach and what their header/close/backdrop add, pre-checked checkbox state, radio state after selection.
tempting_wrong_repair: Run NuExtract in the default look (seconds of latency and a model on the common path); truncate the look silently to max_records or max_bytes; accept where.lines with no look_id, or with an id the server never issued, or with a look of another window; match where.lines against records the look did not display, or against the current lines when the page changed; hand several line matches to the chooser or click the first; allow expect=null on a non-final step; keep executing steps after a non-done one; bind every step selection on the first observation and replay it; guard only the literal control label against destructive verbs; let a confirm field on the press step click whatever dialog appears, or match the confirm label as a prefix, or accept a dialog that shows only part of the record identity; retry a click or the whole plan after a Driver failure; a per-step budget with no plan cap; hints that name a primitive or hand back a fresh look_id the LLM has not seen the lines of; register cua_look only in advanced mode or leave the primitives visible beside it; a harness that makes two calls per scenario by construction.
regression: facade/test_look.py (all): the default look calls no model, shows "half-hour", is read-only, bounded and never silently truncated, focus reports what it filtered out, fields uses the reader once per chunk. facade/test_plan.py (all): whole-plan validation before any Driver action, where.lines needs a matching look_id, page_changed_since_look, fresh observation and new selection per step, stops at the first non-done step, abort_if, destructive guard at validation and at the resolved control, explicit confirm with complete identity, stale recovery inside a step, click never retried, plan budget. facade/test_plan_review.py (all: hidden text, identity tokens and negation, allow_destructive, exact control, page identity, two windows, untrusted text, subtree cache, wording). facade/test_budget.py: test_cua_do_then_cua_look_first_and_every_other_tool_is_opt_in_and_advanced, test_a_third_default_tool_or_a_look_hidden_behind_advanced_fails, test_the_mcp_instructions_describe_only_look_then_do, test_default_workflow_names_cua_look_then_cua_do_and_nothing_else, test_orders_confirm_stays_within_two_calls, test_real_orders_with_the_dialog_follow_up_costs_at_most_two_calls, test_canvas_regions_stays_within_two_calls, test_look_then_plan_is_two_calls_with_no_reader_and_no_chooser_on_the_real_trees, test_the_other_plan_shapes_are_two_calls_measured, test_the_costs_of_skipping_the_look_or_guessing_wrong_are_measured_not_hidden, test_a_stale_page_mid_plan_stops_at_that_step_and_is_budgeted_as_stopped, test_every_plan_scenario_number_is_tied_to_ce_facade_005_and_measured_live_is_not_claimed, test_review_scenarios_show_what_the_guards_cost_when_the_plan_is_wrong, test_a_default_look_that_calls_the_reader_trips_the_reader_budget, test_a_plan_that_secretly_needs_a_second_do_fails_the_budget. facade/check_protocol.py (default surface cua_do, cua_look; advanced 10). scripts/check_call_budget.py. scripts/check_plan_mutations.py (each wrong patch above fails its test by assertion). scripts/look_compare.py and scripts/test_look_compare.py (structure and size only; adjacent_holes: Live capture (2026-09-28) verified real Chrome exposure for 17 pages but NOT dialogs, checkboxes or clicks: see corrected_behavior. The scripted LLM is a LOWER BOUND on the calls a real LLM needs: its phrases come from the goal, so the plan_* ceilings guard call counts, not plan correctness (the plan_booking_vocab_mismatch, plan_hidden_text_negative, plan_negated_dialog and plan_destructive_* scenarios show the cost when the plan is wrong). NOT MEASURED LIVE: no plan has run against a real desktop; every number in the budget is fixture-derived (real captured Chrome trees for booking and orders, synthetic wizard, 100-row list and canvas) and the blind-filter evidence is n=1. NuExtract extraction latency and accuracy on a 100-row page, and whether the deterministic look is good enough there without NuExtract, are unmeasured (scripts/look_compare.py reports structure and bytes only). Whether an LLM writes correct plans (conditions, expects) from a look is unmeasured; the scripted LLM is a lower bound on cost, not evidence of accuracy. Known friction: a type step cannot use the typed text as its expect, so a form plan needs another visible consequence (a live message) or ends delivered_unverified on its last step; a press that opens a dialog needs an expect the LLM must guess before it has seen the dialog (a fragment such as the order number works; a wrong guess stops with confirm_dialog_present and costs a call); an expect that Chrome shows twice (a heading and its text child) is ambiguous and cannot prove a step (the look lists such lines under repeated_text); a where.lines filter over a page that a previous step changed stops page_changed_since_look (a wizard that filters records on every screen needs one plan per screen); several line matches defer rather than choosing; dialog identity is checked by displayed strings, so a dialog that words the identity differently ("Order 1044" vs "#1044") stops with confirm_identity_partial or unknown; dialogs rendered without any new sibling region are not detected as before. A look shows at most 6 lines of 60 characters per record: conditions are evaluated on exactly what was displayed. Plan hints only guide cua_look/cua_do parameters.
invalidation: Withdraw or rework this CE if, measured live on the eval suite, more than a third of the suite tasks cannot be expressed as plans (the LLM cannot write a valid plan from a look, or the grammar cannot state the task), or the wrong-click rate of look-then-plan is above the native arm on the same tasks. n=1 per cell is not a rate: the decision needs the suite run, not the fixture budget.

authority: Proposed; pending user approval. Live probe 2026-09-29 on the repo's own canvas fixtures (user consented), cua-driver 0.30.3, real Chrome, background windows.
classification: projection fix (facade act path) plus a proposed sketch note under S4.2 section 7 / S4.6: delivery of a pixel-addressed click is part of the evidence chain, not assumed.
input_and_actual: Small suite, canvas_regions task, both arms: the click on the drawn Export button was reported delivered (native: effect unverifiable, route accessibility, 'PX hit-test pressed the background element via AX'; stack: driver_call_failed after 1.9 s) and the fixture logged NO press. Probe: with delivery_mode background, cua-driver turns EVERY pixel click (with or without capture_id) into an AX hit-test plus AXPress on the element under the point, i.e. the whole <canvas>; Chrome delivers that press at the element's CENTRE. Second probe, a fixture with one button at the centre and one at a corner: aimed at the corner, the CENTRE button was pressed and the call reported success. So a background pixel click on a drawn surface is a wrong click, not a no-op.
corrected_behavior: A regions-mode selection (perception_region target) is never sent with background delivery: act refuses pointer_not_deliverable_in_background before any Driver call (nothing clicked, the selection given back), and the refusal names the only way through: the caller's explicit allow_foreground (cua_do call, or the plan step) which sets delivery_mode foreground on that click only, so the Driver fronts the window briefly for a real pointer event and restores the previous app. The flag never outlives its call or step, never applies to AX clicks, and false is not permission. No retry ladder: a second background attempt would press the centre again.
tempting_wrong_repair: Retry the same background click (presses the centre again); switch every canvas click to foreground silently (the window-moving behaviour the user forbade); treat effect unverifiable as delivered_unverified (it hides a wrong click); keep a facade-wide flag (the next caller's canvas click would front the window unasked); apply foreground to AX presses too.
regression: facade/test_findings.py CanvasForeground (7 tests: no permission refuses and clicks nothing; false is not permission; permission gives ONE foreground click on the original capture; permission does not outlive the call nor leak into the primitive path; AX presses are never fronted; a plan step carries its own flag; the flag must be true or absent). Five mutations each fail a named test. Budget scenarios canvas_regions, canvas_regions_unique and plan_canvas_look_do carry the flag. experiments/facade-vs-native/pages.py canvas_center is the probe page.
adjacent_holes: Whether the Driver's foreground delivery actually lands a pointer event on a canvas has NOT been run live (the probe covered background only). The Driver behaviour is reported upstream as a bug (a pixel click that resolves to an AXPress loses the point; canvas/WebGL targets need the CGEvent path even in background); if a later driver version delivers background pixel clicks at the point, the refusal should be lifted per driver version, not removed.
invalidation: Withdraw if a live run shows a background pixel click (any driver version this repo pins) landing at the requested point on the canvas_center fixture, or if the foreground click does not land either.

authority: Proposed; pending user approval (user selected option D, browser-first, 2026-09-30). No live evidence yet beyond the observed bypass below.
classification: sketch change (new facade unit of work: the browser tab) plus projection (new default-path capabilities and CALL_BUDGET scenarios). One-way door: public tool surface.
sketch_clause: S4.1 (observation scope), S4.2 section 7 (bounded recovery), S4.6 (independent verification), S4.8 (binding)
input_and_actual: A live agent comparing Amazon listings had to leave cua_look/cua_do to open each product page ("the dispatch tools don't currently support navigation") and used raw Driver browser navigation, so look-before-plan, binding and verification did not apply to any page load. On the Driver's existing-profile refusal it rerouted to a separate browser without asking. Earlier eBay runs: prices visible on the page were absent from the look (AX flattening). The facade's unit is a window with an AXWebArea; most real tasks are multi-page web tasks.
corrected_behavior: The facade treats a browser TAB as the unit of work. (1) cua_look takes {tab} or {url}: with url it opens or reuses a tab in the user's browser profile, waits for ready (existing bounded retry), and verifies the landing (same origin and path as requested, else navigated_elsewhere with the final URL; a login wall is reported, never bypassed); look still never clicks page content. (2) cua_do plans may contain goto {url, expect} and open_tab/close_tab steps, each verified by the resulting page. (3) Observation prefers the Driver's exact CDP binding (DOM text and controls, untrusted_page_text kept) and falls back to the AX tree; both produce the same look shape, and a fact present in one and absent in the other is reported, not silently chosen. (4) A multi-page read (N urls, same fields) is one call returning per-page looks, each with its own look_id. (5) Consent gates (existing-profile grant, allow_foreground) are never rerouted: a refusal returns permission_required naming the grant.
tempting_wrong_repair: Add a lone goto step and keep window-scoped AX-only looks (closes the bypass, keeps the eBay price gap); fall back to a clean browser profile when the user's profile is refused (the reroute this CE forbids); treat 'navigate returned ok' as landing verified (a redirect or login wall is then read as the target page); let look click to dismiss cookie banners (breaks look never clicks); build a free-running browser agent inside the facade (option D of the earlier plan, rejected for per-step model cost).
regression: TO WRITE before code: fixture tests for landing verification (match, redirect, cross-origin, login wall), permission_required on a refused profile, look never clicks with url, DOM/AX disagreement reported, multi-page read budget; CALL_BUDGET scenarios for a 5-listing comparison; check_call_budget.py and check_plan_mutations.py updated.
dissent: (a) Scope: a tab model plus CDP observation is two large changes; ship tab+goto+landing verification first and CDP observation second, behind the same look shape. (b) CDP requires the existing-profile grant, which is now session-only (daemon restarted with --grant existing-profile, no LaunchAgent): a reboot silently returns to AX-only. (c) Using the user's logged-in profile raises the stakes of a wrong click (purchases, messages); the existing confirm step and positive-authorization rules must apply unchanged to every goto that lands on a checkout or account page. (d) Non-Chromium browsers get AX only; Safari users are second-class.
call_budget: New scenarios get their own numbers with changed_by CE-FACADE-007; existing default-path numbers must not move.
